title: Persist review package items alongside their reviewInputDigest
description:
PREREQUISITE of task-4dd4424c1c264f4490bcb7cad01e7585 (Production verifier authority provider), which is itself GAP E of task-97554aa4293e40eab56c0b642e18513a (Foundation self-host canary). Discovered by the worker at 4dd4424c's step-1 authority-matrix gate and re-measured by the architect; it CORRECTS an architect measurement error in that task's planning notes, which wrongly asserted package items were derivable from readReviewLedger.

MEASURED GAP at committed HEAD a42ae2f (git grep / git show against HEAD, not the working tree):

apps/daemon/src/review/review-services.ts submitRound:
  - :112  const itemValues = payloadArray(request.payload, "packageItems")
  - :119  const items = parseItems(itemValues)
  - :123  const built = buildReviewPackage(items)      <- items ARE validated and bound
  - :141  commitAccepted(... eventPayload: { reviewInputDigest, round, route, subjectRef },
                             result: { lineage, reviewInputDigest, round, routing })

The bound items are used to compute `built.value.reviewInputDigest` and are then DISCARDED. Nothing durable retains them.

Corroborating measurements:
- ReviewRoundRecord (apps/daemon/src/review/review-read-model.ts:21-30) carries aggregateVersion, decisionId, lineage, principalId, reviewInputDigest, resultSha256, round, routing -- no items.
- The request bytes are not recoverable either: CommandDecisionRecordBase (packages/store/src/store-contracts.ts:86-106) retains requestSha256 only, never requestBytes.
- buildReviewPackage (packages/review/src/review-package.ts:119-134) requires >=1 CRITERION plus singleton GRAPH_HASH / PLAN_HASH / RUBRIC / SUBMITTED_BYTES / INTEGRATED_TREE.
- Every production instance of those kinds today is a synthetic literal: node-verifier.ts:93-97 PACKAGE_ITEM_FILL (disclosed-synthetic, deliberately out of scope) and apps/control-room/src/live/live-dispatch.ts:144-148 hex64().
- NodeMission is {instructions, test, title, workspace} (apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts:47-52) and carries none of them.

WHY IT BLOCKS. task-4dd4424c must produce VerifierAuthorityFacts.packageItems from a durable record. With the items discarded, the only ways to satisfy it are to mint six 64-hex digests from three scalars, to narrow the DoD, or to reimplement authority inside a test -- all three forbidden by global rail Clause 2 and epic rail 4.

Objective: retain the exact bound package items durably, alongside the reviewInputDigest that already attests them, so a later reader can recover them AND verify them.

Deliverable: submitRound persists the bound items in the same accepted commit as the existing round record, plus a focused durable reader that returns them for a subject/round, plus focused tests. The integrity check is already available and must be used: re-running buildReviewPackage over the restored items must reproduce the stored reviewInputDigest, so a corrupted or substituted item set is detectable rather than merely present.

NOT in scope: changing the ReviewPackageItemInput shape, the REVIEW_PACKAGE_ITEM_KINDS allow-list, buildReviewPackage's rules, the review round lineage/routing semantics, node-verifier's disclosed-synthetic failure-round payload at node-verifier.ts:88-98, or anything under tests/e2e/foundation.

Note for planning: this changes a durable event payload, so it touches the wire/stored shape. Per the epic's verification-budget rule, a schema-shaped change gets full regression at any position -- plan the upcaster/back-compat question explicitly rather than assuming old rounds can be re-read.
definitionOfDone: submitRound durably retains the exact bound package items in the same accepted commit as the round record; a test reads them back for a subject/round and asserts the item set is byte-identical to what was submitted, asserting the items themselves rather than a count.

A durable reader returns the stored items, and re-running buildReviewPackage over them reproduces the stored reviewInputDigest; a test mutates one stored item and asserts the digest comparison refuses with an exact stable code and layer.

A round recorded BEFORE this change (no stored items) reads back as an explicit stable not-found/UNKNOWN code rather than an empty item list -- absent evidence must never present as a valid empty package; a test pins that code and layer.

The existing refusal ordering is preserved: an item set failing buildReviewPackage still refuses at the kernel PACKAGE layer with its original code and writes nothing, proving persistence was added after validation and not in place of it.
A mutation drill removing the persistence makes a NAMED read-back test go red for its item assertion (not for a crash), and production bytes are restored exactly.
pnpm typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm test are exit 0, each printing a nonzero Test Files count line; owned production files are each <=250 physical lines.
taskRails: Fail closed with stable reason codes; a round with no stored items is UNKNOWN, never an empty package, and never gains authority by default.
Do not weaken buildReviewPackage or the REVIEW_PACKAGE_ITEM_KINDS allow-list; persist what validation already bound, after it bound it.
This alters a durable event payload: address back-compatibility for rounds recorded before the change explicitly, and run full regression rather than the owned-package legs alone.
Use TDD. Keep each production source focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400. Stage and commit only explicit owned paths by pathspec; no git add -A, no worktree, no push, no merge.

implementationPlan.description: Confirm the measurement, and note that it NARROWS the task from what the description implies. Read-only. Re-verify each fact on committed HEAD with `git grep`/`git show`, not from this text. (a) THE DISCARD IS REAL: `submitRound` (apps/daemon/src/review/review-services.ts:109-156) parses `packageItems` at :112, binds them through `buildReviewPackage` at :123, and commits at :141 with `eventPayload: {reviewInputDigest, round, route, subjectRef}` and `result: {lineage, reviewInputDigest, round, routing}` -- the items compute the digest and are then dropped. (b) THE REQUEST BYTES ARE NOT A BACK DOOR: `commitAccepted` (bootstrap/bootstrap-ledger.ts:216) does pass `requestBytes` carrying the full payload, but the store only HASHES it -- store-digests.ts:43 and :93 fold it into a digest and `decision-read-decode.ts:101` reads `request_sha256` from the row. There is no request-bytes column. Confirm this yourself; it is the fact that makes the task necessary. (c) THE NARROWING: `committedResultBytes` IS durably persisted (store-input-decision.ts:95-103) and IS read back -- `readReviewLedger` decodes it via `decodeResult` (review-read-model.ts:62) and shapes it in `parseRound` (:150). So the fix belongs in the COMMITTED RESULT, not in a new event payload or a new aggregate: no new event type, no upcaster, and back-compat falls out for free as an explicit absent marker on old rounds. Record this narrowing in the step note, because the task rail written at filing time anticipated an event-payload change plus migration work. The full-regression requirement STAYS (a committed-result shape is still durable state); the migration work does not.

FIVE FACTS THE PLAN DOES NOT STATE, all measured:

1. buildReviewPackage ALSO requires >=1 DAEMON_RECEIPT (review-package.ts:121-123), not just >=1 CRITERION + the five singletons. Fixture packageItems() (review-test-fixtures.ts:189-199) already carries one.

2. admit() SORTS the bound set by canonicalJson([kind,locator,digest]) (review-package.ts:57-79). The BOUND set is therefore order-normalized, not input-ordered, and ReviewPackage exposes no flat list -- only `bound` = {criteria, hashes, receipts, rubric, submittedBytes, tree}. Flattening those six buckets recovers exactly the admitted multiset (every allow-listed kind maps to exactly one bucket). "Byte-identical to what was submitted" is therefore per-item VALUE identity over the same multiset, order-normalized by the kernel. Also makes the step-5 recomputation order-insensitive, which is a property, not an accident.

3. HAZARD -- review-refusal-vocabulary.test.ts:223-228 asserts REVIEW_INGRESS_REFUSAL_CODES + REVIEW_PREREQUISITE_REFUSAL_CODES equals a HAND-WRITTEN 16-entry list, both directions, plus a length check. Adding a restore code to either frozen vocabulary reddens two cases in a file this task does not own. The step-5 helper will carry its OWN frozen code list instead.

4. HAZARD -- tests/security/boundary-roster.security.ts:243 DECLARATION_PATTERN /^export const ([A-Z_]+(?:LAYERS|LAYER|BOUNDARIES))\s*(?::[^=]+)?=/u live-scans production sources against a hand roster with a pinned size. Exporting any const named *_LAYER reddens pnpm test:security, which NO other gate runs (mem:gotcha-new-layer-constant-reddens-boundary-roster). The helper will name its refusing layer via a TYPE, never an exported const.

5. HAZARD -- apps/daemon/src/index-surface.test.ts:343 pins EXPECTED_EXPORTS.length === 85 against Object.keys(daemon) (RUNTIME keys only; `export type` is invisible). So the helper must NOT be added to apps/daemon/src/index.ts. It does not need to be: in-daemon consumers use relative imports (node-verifier.ts:11 imports readReviewLedger from "../review/review-read-model.js"), and task-4dd4424c's target VerifierAuthorityFacts already lives in apps/daemon/src/review/verifier-receipt-ledger.ts -- same directory.

Read-only step; no files modified.

NOTE: `review-read-model.ts` has NO test file of its own today -- the review suites are review-acceptance, review-delta, review-lineage, review-refusal-vocabulary, review-services and verifier-receipt-ledger. Create apps/daemon/src/review/review-read-model.test.ts. Result: `Test Files 1 failed (1) / Tests 3 failed (3)` -- all three fail as ASSERTIONS (not crashes), each because the field does not exist yet:

1. "hands back the exact package items a stored round carries, item by item" -- expected {items, status:"PRESENT"}, received undefined.

DESIGN CHOSEN FOR THE ABSENT MARKER, and why it is stronger than the plan's minimum: `packageItems` is a DISCRIMINATED UNION, `{items, status:"PRESENT"} | {status:"ABSENT"}`, not `T[] | undefined`. Consequence: `?? []` cannot apply (never nullish), a spread `[...record.packageItems]` does not typecheck, and `.length` does not exist without narrowing on `.status`. The empty-array disguise the plan's risk section calls load-bearing is therefore structurally unreachable, not merely untaken. Case 2 pins it three ways: not `[]`, not `{items:[],status:"PRESENT"}`, not `{items:[],status:"ABSENT"}`.

MALFORMED SWEEP: 11 hand-written cases (object-not-array, bare string, non-object element, missing digest, missing locator, non-hex digest, 63-char digest, non-string locator, kind outside the allow-list, forbidden kind, extra key). The count is asserted nonzero AND pinned at 11 before the loop runs, so a sweep that silently produced zero cases cannot pass. Each case asserts the STABLE CODE AND THE LAYER by driving a real `review.submit` afterwards: `REVIEW_LINEAGE_UNREADABLE` refused by `DAEMON_PREREQUISITE`, not merely `unreadable === true`.

Case 2 also asserts `ledger.unreadable === false` for a pre-change round: absent must be READABLE-and-marked, otherwise every round recorded before today is stranded.

Case 1 asserts twice on purpose -- once against a hand-written seven-item literal (no shared operand; an eighth fixture item cannot appear on both sides) and once against the array actually staged into the durable bytes (so the literal cannot drift into asserting a set nothing stores).

implementationPlan.description: The integrity check -- what turns 'the items are present' into 'the items are the right ones'. Add a production helper that reads a stored round's items and re-runs the PUBLIC `buildReviewPackage` from bare `@moe/review` over them, comparing the recomputed `reviewInputDigest` against the digest ALREADY STORED on that round. Put it in production where the eventual consumer can call it -- task-4dd4424c must perform this check outside a test, and a verification that exists only in a test file gives the consumer nothing. Test it both ways: an accepted control where the recomputation matches, and a negative where one stored item's digest is mutated in the durable bytes and the comparison must DISAGREE and refuse with an exact stable code and layer (assert both literals). Include the accepted control deliberately: a refusal-only suite cannot see a wrong ACCEPTED value.
implementationPlan.note:
RED then GREEN. RED was a genuine module-absent failure -- `Error: Cannot find module './review-package-restore.js'`, `Tests no tests` -- then GREEN at `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 8 passed (8)`. Whole src/review slice: `Test Files 9 passed (9) / Tests 95 passed (95)`. apps/daemon tsc exit 0.

PRODUCTION, in production, not in a test: apps/daemon/src/review/review-package-restore.ts (120 lines) plus its `.js` bridge. Two exported entry points, because task-4dd4424c's call site (node-verifier.ts:135-137) ALREADY holds the ledger and the round record:
- `verifyStoredPackageItems(record: ReviewRoundRecord)` -- the check itself, no store scan.
- `restoreReviewPackage(store, projectId, subjectRef, round)` -- the ledger-reading entry.
A store-only API would force that consumer into a second full decision-log scan to ask one question about a round it already has.

THE CHECK: recompute with the kernel's PUBLIC `buildReviewPackage` over the restored items, compare against `record.reviewInputDigest` -- the value the HANDLER stored at submit time. Recomputed-against-STORED. The tautology drill (step 6, drill 3) targets exactly this line.

REFUSAL ORDER, and why: unreadable -> not-found -> absent -> kernel-refusal -> digest-mismatch. Unreadable precedes the round lookup deliberately: `readReviewLedger` DROPS a round it cannot parse, so a wanted round whose bytes were rejected would otherwise read as "not found". Two different facts must not share one code.

FOUR OWN CODES, in a frozen `REVIEW_PACKAGE_RESTORE_CODES`: REVIEW_PACKAGE_DIGEST_MISMATCH, REVIEW_PACKAGE_ITEMS_ABSENT, REVIEW_PACKAGE_ROUND_NOT_FOUND, REVIEW_PACKAGE_ROUND_UNREADABLE. Deliberately NOT added to REVIEW_INGRESS/PREREQUISITE_REFUSAL_CODES -- those describe what the review COMMAND surface emits, and review-refusal-vocabulary.test.ts:223-228 asserts them equal a hand-written 16-entry list in both directions, so appending would have reddened a file this task does not own (measured at step 1).

EIGHT CASES, each pinning a code AND a layer:
1. ACCEPTED CONTROL (load-bearing per the step): an honest round restores ok, items equal a hand-written seven-item literal in bind order, and `reviewInputDigest` equals the digest the production handler stored. A refuse-everything implementation would satisfy every negative below and fail only this.
2. DIGEST SUBSTITUTION: one stored item's digest swapped for another VALID 64-hex -- the set still binds cleanly, nothing structural is wrong, only the recomputation notices. REVIEW_PACKAGE_DIGEST_MISMATCH @ DAEMON_PREREQUISITE, kernelLayer null.
3. LOCATOR SUBSTITUTION, digest untouched: same code and layer. Proves the digest covers the locator, not only the digests.
4. KERNEL PASSTHROUGH: a restored set missing its DAEMON_RECEIPT refuses with the KERNEL's own PACKAGE_BINDING_INCOMPLETE @ refusedBy REVIEW_KERNEL, kernelLayer PACKAGE -- so validity is still the kernel's question, not this module's and not the read model's.
5. ABSENT: a pre-change round refuses REVIEW_PACKAGE_ITEMS_ABSENT @ DAEMON_PREREQUISITE, and is asserted NOT to equal an ok-with-empty-items result.
6. NOT FOUND: round 7 against a store holding only round 1.
7. UNREADABLE: a malformed items key.
8. VOCABULARY, both directions against a HAND-WRITTEN list, so a fifth code cannot appear on both sides and stay green.

Cases 2-4 all stage against the FIRST round's genuine production digest (`stageAgainstHonestDigest`): the digest operand is real handler output and only the items are tampered with, which is the substitution the check exists to catch. A hand-written digest on both sides would have proved nothing.

implementationPlan.description: Mutation drills, three, one per distinct claim. Drill 1 (persistence is real): remove the items from the `result` object in review-services.ts; the step-4 read-back test must go RED on its item-value assertion, not on a crash. Drill 2 (absent is not empty): make the read model return `[]` instead of the absent marker when the items key is missing; the step-2 case (2) test must go RED. This is the load-bearing drill -- an empty array is precisely how absent evidence passes as a valid package. Drill 3 (the digest binding is real): make the step-5 comparison compare the recomputed digest against a digest recomputed from the same restored items instead of against the STORED digest -- the classic tautology with both operands from one source; the mutated-item test must go RED. If drill 3 stays green the check is comparing the items to themselves and must be rewritten. Record for each drill the command, the failing test NAME and the exact assertion. Restore by re-editing, never `git checkout` (destructive in this shared worktree), and confirm with `git diff --numstat` showing 0 added and 0 deleted per drilled file. One drill at a time -- a peer commit landing mid-drill can swallow the patch and leave git reading clean.

[]`, no spread, no default parameter, and none is expressible -- the field is a discriminated union, never nullish.

ONE GAP THE PLAN DID NOT NAME, FOUND AND CLOSED. A deliberately stored `packageItems: []` parses as PRESENT-and-empty (it IS structurally present), so the read model alone would hand a caller a well-formed zero-evidence package. No handler can write it -- `buildReviewPackage` refuses an empty set at submit time -- so it is only reachable by tampering with durable bytes. Added a case asserting the kernel denies it authority: `PACKAGE_BINDING_INCOMPLETE` at refusedBy REVIEW_KERNEL, kernelLayer PACKAGE. Suite now 97 passing.

ONE THEORETICAL RISK, DISCLOSED, NOT FIXED. This enlarges the committed result. `decodeBoundedJsonBytes` caps a decoded body at MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES = 1_048_576 (packages/contracts/src/input-limits.ts:1); MAX_COMMIT_BYTES is 32 MiB, so the 1 MiB decode bound binds first. A submit carrying a near-1 MiB item set plus a grown lineage could produce a result that no longer decodes on read. Behaviour is FAIL-CLOSED (decodeResult -> null -> parseRound undefined -> unreadable -> REVIEW_LINEAGE_UNREADABLE, no authority), and the growth vector already existed via the lineage, but this change raises the rate. Realistic sets are ~110 bytes/item, so the seven-item fixture adds ~800 bytes. Capping the set would need a new refusal code and a policy decision, which is outside this task's stated scope -- flagging for the architect rather than inventing a bar.

Also checked and clear: determinism (bind order is the kernel's sort then its six slots, so identical requests still produce identical result bytes -- the replay/resultSha256 case stays green); the returned items array and each item are frozen, so a reader cannot mutate the restored set; every test file closes its SQLite handles via `afterEach(closeStores)`.

planningNotes.risks: The load-bearing risk is the empty-array disguise: if an absent item set reads back as `[]`, a consumer sees a well-formed package with zero evidence and cannot tell it from a real one -- that is how absent evidence gains authority, which epic rail 4 forbids. Drill 2 pins it. Second, a tautological integrity check: recomputing the digest from restored items and comparing against a digest recomputed the same way proves nothing; the comparison must be against the digest STORED on the round at submit time, and drill 3 proves it is. Third, persist the BOUND items, not the raw parsed array -- pre-validation bytes would be durably recorded without the stored digest attesting them. Fifth, rejecting a malformed items key makes the whole round unreadable -- the correct fail-closed choice, but it can strand existing history, so state the trade rather than discovering it. Sixth, this is durable state: full regression is required, and root `pnpm test` does NOT cover apps/**, so the filtered daemon leg is not redundant.
